# ops map CLI fixtures (hammer-ai-ops-cli-map-commands)

Sealed-room numbers are the QuickPlay / IssueEngine sealed room: interior
256x256x128, walls/floor/ceiling 16 thick, player start `(0, 0, 32)`, one
`light` at `(0, 0, 100)`. Generated by a script (plane-point winding gives
outward normals); do not hand-edit — regenerate instead.

- `sealed-room.vmf` — 6 box brushes, player start + light. Validates clean,
  builds sealed, compiles on all three presets.
- `sealed-room.map` — the same room as Valve 220 .map (same 6 brushes,
  same 2 entities). Validates clean; proves the .map load path.
- `leaking-room.vmf` — the +X wall split in two with a 1-unit gap at
  y in [-0.5, 0.5]. Mirrors IssueEngineTests.LeakRoom exactly: exactly one
  LEAK issue, build exits 1 (`leak`), compile exits 1 (`leak`).
- `no-spawn-room.vmf` — the sealed room with no info_player_start. Build
  exits 1 (`no-player-start`); compile exits 1 (`missing-player-start`).

## Seam (also in OpsCli.cs header)

- `BuildScript.Map.cs` (worker 64) does NOT exist on disk yet. Until it
  lands, `map build <script>` runs whatever BuildScript verbs exist via
  ScriptLive; the CLI calls the native kernel APIs directly (QuickPlay /
  CompileRunner / IssueEngine / MapBakeExport) and never shells out to
  Hammer/VBSP/VVIS/VRAD.
- MapDocument HAS landed (2026-11-13 16:28: MapDocument.cs + MapDocumentIo.cs)
  but MapDocumentIo reads/writes .gmap ONLY — no VMF/.map import — and
  MapDocument has exactly one kernel projection (ToIssueDocument). There is
  no VmfDocument -> MapDocument import and no MapDocument -> CompileInput /
  QuickPlayMap / MapBakeDocument projection anywhere, so the CLI projects
  VmfDocument onto each kernel input type directly. When a VmfDocument ->
  MapDocument import lands, validate/issues can route through
  MapDocument.ToIssueDocument and the other projections collapse to
  MapDocument -> kernel type.
- `map issues` exits 0 whenever the check ran (a listing); `map validate`
  exits 1 on any error-severity issue (a gate).
- Known losses, reported in the export JSON, never silent: per-face Valve
  UV axes are not projected (default UV on obj/glb); displacement offsets
  are not projected (flat brush faces bake); only point `light` entities
  project to CompileLight; GLB export is the minimal writer (GlbNote).
